NDT training in Birmingham, AL: how it works

Short answer: Birmingham technicians study NDT theory self-paced on the Atlantis online portal, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions from the moment they enroll. They practice in the Practical NDT browser simulator and build hands-on skill in person at their employer's mill, plant or fabrication shop. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Birmingham. Employers certify technicians under ASNT SNT-TC-1A written practices; ASNT central exams are the other route.

Birmingham was built on iron and steel, and metal still drives most of its inspection work. Pipe and tube makers, steel mills, structural steel fabricators and foundries line the Jones Valley, and the headquarters of the region's largest utility and its nuclear operating company are downtown. A technician in Jefferson County is more likely to inspect welds on fabricated steel, pipe in a mill or components in a power plant than anything offshore, and that shapes which methods matter most.

The training is set up for people already working or about to start. Theory is self-paced on the portal and fits around shifts. The practical ability comes from supervised work on real parts at a Birmingham-area employer, logged against its written practice. That employer then examines and certifies you.

Ask about NDT training in Birmingham and include the methods, levels and number of people you need trained. We reply within one business day.

How to get NDT certified in Birmingham: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Fabricators, mills, inspection companies and plant contractors in the Birmingham area generally certify to written practices based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The path looks like this.

  1. Get a copy of the written practice your employer uses. It covers each method and level and sets the training hours, experience hours, examinations and vision checks. If you are still looking for work, the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows what most programs expect.
  2. Finish formal training on the portal for your method and level. Recommended minimum hours appear in the training requirements matrix.
  3. Log supervised experience on welds, pipe or castings with a certified Level II or III, and have each entry signed.
  4. Pass the general examination, a written test of the method's theory, equipment and terms.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the employer's procedures and acceptance standards, for example AWS D1.1 for a structural fabricator or a product specification at a pipe mill.
  6. Pass the practical examination on representative specimens, graded by or under a Level III.
  7. Pass vision testing for near-vision acuity and color contrast as the written practice requires.
  8. Receive certification from your employer, which signs the record and keeps it.
  9. Recertify at the interval in the written practice; SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum of five years.

Technicians who want a credential independent of any one company can prepare for ASNT central certification, ASNT 9712 for Level I and II or the ASNT NDT Level III examinations, and Atlantis prepares candidates for those too. The employer's role is set out on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Birmingham technicians

All courses follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge. Start with Level 1 training, add Level 2 training once your hours allow, and look at Level III preparation when you are ready to run a program. The table shows how each method is used in the Birmingham area.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Birmingham
VTVisual acuity, lighting, weld gauges and visual acceptance criteriaStructural steel and bridge welds at fabricators, receiving inspection, plant maintenance
MTYoke, prod and bench techniques, field direction, particles and demagnetizationFillet and groove welds on structural steel, castings and forgings, rotating equipment parts
UTCalibration, straight-beam and angle-beam techniques, thickness gauging, reportingComplete-joint-penetration welds in buildings and bridges, pipe and tube inspection, thickness checks in power plants
PAUT and TOFDPhased-array focal laws, encoded scanning, TOFD, analysis and sizing for UT Level II techniciansHeavy-wall welds and power plant components where the owner's specification allows advanced UT
RTExposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital radiography, interpretationCastings, pressure piping and vessel welds at shops with a radiography license
PTCleaning, penetrant application and dwell, removal, developer, interpretationNon-magnetic castings and machined parts, stainless piping, valve components
ETImpedance-plane analysis, probes, calibration and tubing or surface techniquesCondenser and heat-exchanger tubing at power plants, surface crack checks on components

Level III preparation covers the ASNT Basic and Method examinations and gives practice in writing procedures and examinations. In Birmingham it is usually taken by a fabricator's or mill's quality manager, or by a senior technician at an inspection company who will sign off its program.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Birmingham

UT is in steady demand in Birmingham because of structural steel. Building codes and bridge specifications require examination of complete-joint-penetration welds, and on thicker sections that examination is usually ultrasonic. A fabricator's UT technician needs to calibrate to the code, scan groove welds from the right faces, evaluate indications against the code's acceptance tables and write a report the engineer of record will accept. The UT training course covers those skills, along with straight-beam work for laminations and thickness.

Even so, the methods used most across Birmingham's fabrication shops are VT and MT. Visual inspection comes first on every weld, and MT is the standard surface method for carbon steel structures and castings. A new technician will usually be certified in VT and MT before moving to UT.

Where NDT technicians work around Birmingham

Pipe, tube and steel production. American Cast Iron Pipe Company and McWane are both headquartered in Birmingham and make pipe and related products. Nucor runs a steel mill in the city, and U.S. Steel's Fairfield Works, to the west, makes seamless tubular products. Mills and pipe plants use automated inspection systems backed by technicians in UT, MT, VT and ET.

Structural steel fabrication. Birmingham has a long tradition of structural and miscellaneous steel fabrication for buildings, bridges and industrial plants across the Southeast. Fabricators inspect to AWS D1.1, and to AWS D1.5 for bridge work, with VT, MT and UT.

Power generation. Alabama Power and Southern Company are headquartered in Birmingham, and Southern Nuclear, which operates the company's nuclear plants, is based in the city. Fossil plants nearby, including the Miller plant in west Jefferson County, bring outage work: UT thickness, ET on condenser tubes, MT and PT. Nuclear in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI, and nuclear UT usually requires performance demonstration qualification on top of SNT-TC-1A training, with access controlled by the utility.

Foundries and heavy manufacturing. Foundries, forging shops and machine shops in the region inspect castings and forgings with MT, PT, RT and UT.

Automotive supply chain. The Mercedes-Benz plant at Vance in Tuscaloosa County and other vehicle plants in Alabama draw suppliers that inspect welded and cast parts, mostly with VT, MT and UT.

NDT schools and classes near Birmingham: what to compare

Looking for NDT classes near Birmingham, you will see community college welding and industrial maintenance programs, schools in other states and online courses that combine self-paced theory with a practical at an employer. Any of these can work, provided the training record will meet the written practice of the company that certifies you.

  • Which standard is the course based on, and does the completion record state method, level and hours?
  • Who is the Level III responsible for the material, and in which methods is that Level III certified?
  • How is the practical handled, and will you inspect welds, castings and pipe like those made in Birmingham?
  • Does the course prepare you for employer examinations, ASNT central examinations or both?
  • What will you be able to show a new employer if you change jobs?

The Atlantis model: self-paced theory on the portal with Level III Q&A, simulator practice in the browser, and the hands-on practical and practical examination in person at the employer's facility under its written practice. The published US fees for every course are listed in the table on this page, and Register & Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal. More answers are on the NDT training FAQ.

Online NDT training in Alabama

Mill and plant schedules in Alabama often involve rotating shifts and overtime during outages. Self-paced theory suits that: on the Atlantis portal you study when you can, go back over what you need and send questions to the Level III. There is no class time to keep.

The practical portion cannot be done online. Alabama employers certify after supervised hands-on experience and a practical examination on real parts. For the rest of the state, see NDT training in Alabama; the national overview is on NDT training in the USA.

Training a crew at your Birmingham facility (employers)

A Birmingham fabricator, mill or inspection company that needs several people qualified can have them complete theory online, then carry out hands-on training and practical examinations in person at its own facility, using its own equipment and parts. The specific examination can then follow the employer's procedures and the acceptance criteria in its customers' specifications.

Fabricators and mills also face customer and registrar audits. Written practice development brings the program document into line with the methods you actually perform, and ASNT Level III consulting can review procedures, prepare and grade examinations and check certification files. Group options are on the corporate NDT training page.

Radiography licensing in Alabama

Alabama is an NRC Agreement State, so radiography in Birmingham is regulated by the Alabama Department of Public Health's Office of Radiation Control. Companies that use radiography sources or industrial X-ray equipment must be licensed or registered with the state, and the people who operate that equipment must hold the radiation safety certification Alabama's rules require. Check the Office of Radiation Control's current guidance on which certifications it accepts and how out-of-state crews can work in Alabama.

None of this is part of an NDT method course. Radiographic testing training covers technique and interpretation for SNT-TC-1A certification, while radiation safety certification runs through the employer's licensed program. Birmingham radiographers need both.

Practice before your practical exam

Practical NDT is a browser simulator for rehearsing inspections. Birmingham trainees usually get the most from the welding workshop, the magnetic particle simulator and the UT simulator. Simulator practice helps with setups and interpretation, but it is not logged experience and does not replace the practical examination on real parts.

Check your theory with the free practice tests, or try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Birmingham

How long does it take to get NDT certified in Birmingham, Alabama?

The written practice decides. Theory can be completed in weeks, but the supervised experience hours for each level take longer, and those set the pace.

How much does NDT training cost in Birmingham?

The published US fees for each course are in the table on this page. For a group at a Birmingham employer, contact us and we reply within one business day.

Can I take NDT training online in Alabama?

Yes, the theory is online and self-paced. The practical and the practical examination are done in person at your employer.

Is there an NDT school near me in Birmingham?

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Birmingham or elsewhere in Alabama. Theory is online, and hands-on work happens at the employer's facility. Use the checklist above to compare local options.

Which NDT method should I learn first in Birmingham?

VT and MT, because structural steel fabrication and casting inspection rely on them. UT is the natural next step.

Are there NDT jobs in Birmingham?

Pipe and steel producers, structural fabricators, foundries, power plants and inspection contractors all employ NDT technicians in the Birmingham area.

Do I need CWI as well as NDT certification?

Some fabricators also ask for AWS Certified Welding Inspector for welding inspection roles. It is a separate credential; Atlantis courses cover the NDT methods.

Does my certification transfer to another Birmingham employer?

Not automatically. Your next Jefferson County employer looks over your training, experience and exam records, then issues its own certification under its written practice. ASNT central certification moves with you.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Birmingham?

Yes, online. See ASNT Level III training.

Who is the instructor?

Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with more than eleven years of international field experience.
